We got search results: two templates. Need to return the mapped_rxn associated with the template that, when applied to the molecule, reproduces the reaction described. Which template is appropriate? The first template (reaction_id 214705) seems to be a sulfonamide formation from sulfonyl chloride and amine? Let's examine its retro_smarts_template: '[O;D1;H0:2]=[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])(-[c:4])-[NH;D2;+0:5]-[c:6]>>O-[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])(=[O;D1;H0:3])-[c:4].[NH2;D1;+0:5]-[c:6]'

This is a retrosynthetic direction: product (sulfonamide) -> sulfonyl chloride + amine. That matches our forward reaction: amine attacks sulfonyl chloride to give sulfonamide. So this template is appropriate.

The second template seems to involve Cl-C(=O)-aryl and SH (thiol) to give sulfonyl chloride? Not relevant.

Thus we should return mapped_rxn from first template. The mapped_rxn string is given in result. Let's extract it.

From result: first entry's 'mapped_rxn' is:

'[CH3:1][CH2:2][CH2:3][N:4]1[C:5](=[O:6])[C:7]2=[C:8]([N:9]=[C:10](/[CH:11]=[CH:12]/[C:13]3=[CH:14][C:15]([O:16][CH3:17])=[C:18]([O:19][CH3:20])[CH:21]=[C:22]3[S:23](=[O:24])(=[O:25])O)[N:33]2[CH3:34])[N:35]([CH2:36][CH2:37][CH3:38])[C:39]1=[O:40].[NH2:26][C:27]1=[CH:28][CH:29]=[CH:30][CH:31]=[CH:32]1>>[CH3:1][CH2:2][CH2:3][N:4]1[C:5](=[O:6])[C:7]2=[C:8]([N:9]=[C:10](/[CH:11]=[CH:12]/[C:13]3=[CH:14][C:15]([O:16][CH3:17])=[C:18]([O:19][CH3:20])[CH:21]=[C:22]3[S:23](=[O:24])(=[O:25])[NH:26][C:27]3=[CH:28][CH:29]=[CH:30][CH:31]=[CH:32]3)[N:33]2[CH3:34])[N:35]([CH2:36][CH2:37][CH3:38])[C:39]1=[O:40]'

We also need template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). The result includes 'reaction_id' and 'template_hash'. Which is template_id? The description says "template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash)". In search results, there is 'reaction_id' maybe corresponds to template ID? Usually template_id is separate. But likely they want the 'reaction_id' as template_id. We'll use 214705.
